tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Query authoritative DNS records (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CNAME, NS, SOA) for a domain via RFC-compliant DNS-over-HTTPS.

tools.name: mx_lookup
tools.description: Query designated mail exchange (MX) servers, priority ranking, and target IP addresses for an email domain.

tools.name: spf_check
tools.description: Inspect domain Sender Policy Framework (SPF) TXT records, parsed mechanisms, include counts, and RFC 7208 lookup limits.

tools.name: dmarc_check
tools.description: Inspect domain DMARC email spoofing policy (none, quarantine, reject), percentage enforcement, and aggregate reporting tags.

tools.name: security_headers_check
tools.description: Audit HTTP security response headers including HSTS, Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Frame-Options, and Permissions-Policy with posture scoring.

tools.name: whois_lookup
tools.description: Query authoritative ICANN RDAP domain registration date, expiry date, registrar name, nameservers, and status codes.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: dmarc_check · Private data: dns_lookup, spf_check · Public sink: mx_lookup, dmarc_check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: dmarc_check · Private data: dns_lookup, spf_check · Public sink: mx_lookup, dmarc_check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
